questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Molecular Orbital Theory Bond Orders & Magnetism
questions.category: Chemical Bonding & Molecular Structure :: Quantitative & Structural Chemistry (Type 1)
questions.question: According to Molecular Orbital Theory in [Chemical Bonding & Molecular Structure], which of the following diatomic species has a bond order of $2.5$ and is paramagnetic with one unpaired electron?
questions.solution: $\text{O}_2^+$ has 15 electrons. Configuration: $\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \sigma_{2p_z}^2 (\pi_{2p_x}^2 = \pi_{2p_y}^2) (\pi_{2p_x}^{*1})$. Bond order $= \frac{10 - 5}{2} = 2.5$. It has one unpaired electron in $\pi^*$ and is paramagnetic.
questions.explanation: Analyze using fundamental chemical principles in Chemical Bonding & Molecular Structure.
tags: Molecular Orbital Theory Bond Orders & Magnetism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Molecular Orbital Theory Bond Orders & Magnetism
questions.category: Chemical Bonding & Molecular Structure :: Quantitative Chemistry
questions.question: In [Chemical Bonding & Molecular Structure], what is the number of lone pairs of electrons located on the central xenon atom in xenon tetrafluoride $(\text{XeF}_4)$?
questions.solution: Xenon has 8 valence electrons. Four form single bonds with fluorine atoms, leaving $8 - 4 = 4$ non-bonding electrons, which correspond to $2$ lone pairs (square planar geometry, $sp^3d^2$).
questions.explanation: Calculate using quantitative laws in Chemical Bonding & Molecular Structure.
tags: Molecular Orbital Theory Bond Orders & Magnetism
